title: Input signalizer: Unicode skim and shared short-input cache for low-latency preflight
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: A large portion of request latency on short prompts (<64 tokens) is dominated by prefill-side preprocessing: normalization, tokenization warmups, and routing into kernel/attention variants. Current pipeline performs full UTF-8 normalization and tokenization on every request, causing overhead spikes and preventing effective microbatching for small, high-QPS traffic.

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'input signalizer' micro-pass that quickly classifies an incoming prompt and routes it to the lowest-cost fast path when safe. The signalizer will: 1) perform a SIMD-accelerated ASCII/UTF-8 skim to detect simple ASCII-only inputs, 2) compute a compact stable hash for a short-input shared cache (e.g., prompts <= 128 bytes), and 3) emit routing metadata (fastlane, normalization-needed, likely token-count) to the prefill scheduler and kernel selector.

Why this matters: By routing ASCII/simple inputs into a specialized normalization-free fastlane and serving cached tokenized prefixes for frequent short prompts, we expect to reduce median prefill overhead by 40-70% and 95th-percentile by 20-40ms on busy workloads. This complements existing kernel selection and attention optimizations by ensuring decode scheduling and KV-cache prewarm decisions operate with accurate, low-latency signals.
acceptance_criteria: Signalizer classification introduces <0.5ms median overhead on representative CPU configs
ASCII fastlane end-to-end median prefill time reduces by >=40% for short prompts (<64 tokens)
Shared short-input cache hit rate >= 15% on internal chatbot benchmark; misses fall back to existing pipeline
No functional change for non-ASCII inputs (full normalization + tokenization path remains default)
Telemetry added: classification breakdown, cache hit/miss, fallback reasons, memory usage
implementation_steps: Prototype SIMD UTF-8/ASCII skim using existing vector utils (C++ runtime) and benchmark micro-latency
Design compact short-input cache key: stable hash over normalized minimal representation + model+version+route
Implement thread-safe LRU cache with bounded memory and eviction metrics (configurable per deployment tier)
Expose signalizer outputs in prefill scheduler API so kernel selector and KV prewarm can consume flags
Add server-side safety checks: collision avoidance thresholds, privacy scrub for PII-sensitive routes, TTLs
Run canary on internal runtime cluster with synthetic and production-like traffic; collect metrics and compare against baseline
Iterate: tune cache size, hash function, classification thresholds; add config flags for dedicated/private customers
metrics: Median prefill-side latency (ms) - target -40% on short prompts
Short-input cache hit rate (%) - target >= 15% on target workloads
Signalizer CPU cycles per request - target median < 0.5ms
Memory used by short-input cache (MB) and eviction rate
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Patel: Spike prototype completed. SIMD skim reduces header pass by ~0.6ms on c5d-like instances. Initial hash function (xxh64) shows low collision in synthetic corpus.

2026-03-03 - Diego Alvarez: Reviewed prototype. Concern: current cache key included raw prompt which could surface PII. Added privacy scrub step - canonicalize whitespace and redact long numeric sequences before hashing.
2026-03-05 - PM review (Alisha Rao): Suggest exposing cache control via Console feature flag for Dedicated customers to opt into shared cache; enterprise compliance may require auditability.
2026-03-08 - Benchmark run: internal chatbot trace shows 18% cache hit rate, median prefill drop from 1.8ms -> 0.9ms for short prompts. 95th tail improved by ~22ms on synthetic burst test.

2026-03-10 - Security (Jordan Li): Quick review OK but flagged need for full security_review_required gating before Private release. See linked notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-70199-signalizer
